narrative.overview:
The store is a toy valley at dusk seen through a vine-framed window. The fire logo tile rises over the hills like the sun, embers drift up from it, toy silhouettes (a bear on the left hill, a block tower and a rocket on the right) stand on the ridges, and the catalog below reads like a game's world index: Lilita One category tabs between hairlines broken by a single dot, and framed card wells that are each a small piece of the valley at their category's hour of day.

The ground is near-black pine, never white. Light comes from two sources only: the authored dusk scene and fire. Fire is rationed: the gradient belongs to the logo tile, and one flat fire-orange action with dark ink leads each view. Everything else is white ink, sage and moss on pine, with hairline structure instead of boxed sections.

Confirmed rejection: the white e-commerce grid with a banner carousel.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black pine ground with pine surfaces one and two steps lighter; 1px hairlines broken by a single dot.
Lilita One display in white, moss for inactive tabs and the footer wordmark; Nunito body in sage or ink.
One flat fire-orange action per view with fire-ink text; the fire gradient only on the logo tile.
Card image wells with hand-cut organic corners and a 2px moss rim, each holding a per-category valley scene.
Category colours only as icon tint and small dots, never as fills.
An authored SVG valley whose hills, vines and grass are anchored to the frame's edges, with pointer parallax and rising embers that stop under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Fire Rule
rules.body: Each view carries exactly one filled fire-orange action with fire-ink text. Other fire on screen (count badge, seal, icon, caret, selection, hover text) points at that same purchase path and is never a second action. A secondary choice beside it is outlined (Comprobante, Volver).

rules.name: The Fire Tile Rule
rules.body: The gold-orange-red fire gradient lives only on the logo tile and the favicon. Buttons, badges and the seal use flat fire. The valley's own dusk gradients (sky, sun halo, hills) are scene light, not UI fill.

rules.name: The Dots and Tints Rule
rules.body: On pine, a category colour appears only as the toy icon's tint inside a card well and as the 10px dot on a season pill. It is never a block, band or panel; panel-style category fills do not cross into the store. The shipped sale sticker (a coral disc on discounted cards) is a known divergence from this rule, not a pattern to extend.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Lilita One speaks for whatever a family reads as a name or acts on: titles, tabs, prices, totals, numerals, links and every button label. Nunito carries descriptions, meta, field text and labels. Lilita has one weight; never synthesise bold on it.

rules.name: The White, Moss, Sage Rule
rules.body: Titles and active states are white ink; inactive tabs, the footer wordmark and footer links are moss; supporting copy is sage. Body Nunito never drops below 600.

rules.name: The Glow, Not Slab Rule
rules.body: In El valle, anything raised casts a blurred shadow or a warm glow; a hard offset base never appears, including under the logo tile.

dos: Do keep the store on pine ground (sw-ground) with pine surface and raised steps; never introduce a white or light surface.
Do give each view exactly one flat fire-orange action with fire-ink Lilita text, and outline any choice beside it.
Do separate sections with the rule-dot divider and move the dot between placements rather than adding boxes or borders.
Do set titles, tabs, prices, links and button labels in Lilita One; descriptions, meta and labels in Nunito 600 to 800.
Do frame every product image in an organic well with the 2px moss rim, alternating the two organic radii.
Do show category only as icon tint and small dots, and give photo-less products their category's CardScene.
Do anchor scene pieces that carry meaning (hills, toys, vines) to the frame's edges so they survive narrow widths, and keep hero text inside the deep-blue band of the sky.
Do stop parallax, embers and twinkle under reduced motion, and keep the ember focus ring on every focusable element.
donts: Don't build the white e-commerce grid with a banner carousel.
Don't use the fire gradient anywhere but the logo tile and favicon.
Don't put a second filled fire action in the same view, or set text other than fire-ink on fire.
Don't fill tabs, cards, bands or panels with category colours.
Don't give anything in the store a hard zero-blur offset shadow, including the logo tile.
Don't replace the authored valley with a raster or stock image.
Don't carry panel rules into the store (sol as position marker, category fills, the board-space track); this world has its own.

narrative.overview:
Every incoming shipment is a game in progress. The lote is a track of flat, category-coloured board spaces; each saved product fills the next space with its category's colour and the token hops forward toward the sun-yellow goal flag. The rest of the app is the same table seen from other angles: warm off-white card stock on which rounded surfaces rest, a deep teal rail along the edge like the side of the box, flat colour casillas that always mean a category, and figures that never jiggle.

Density is operational, not playful-loose: the employee is loading fifty products in five minutes with a scanner and the keyboard. Playfulness lives in material and motion (heavy rounded type, flat fills, spring hops, cards dropping onto a stack), never in extra steps or decorative chrome. Controls are standard web controls in board-game clothing.

The confirmed anti-reference is the category default: a grey data table with one blue accent and a generic progress bar.

Two worlds. This file records two route-scoped visual worlds. Everything from here through the first Do's and Don'ts is the staff panel's "Tablero de juego" (inventory, quick-add, suppliers, categories, reports, sign-in). The customer store at /tienda is a second world, "El valle", user-pinned on 2026-11-03 and recorded in its own part at the end of this file (tokens prefixed `sw-` and `store-`). Panel rules (The Board Space Rule, The Fixed Board Rule, The Sol Marks Here Rule, The Heavy Ink Rule, The Still Figures Rule, The Table-Top Rule, The One Piece Rule) govern the panel only; El valle has its own rules. The worlds share the logo tile, the Nunito body family, tabular figures (`.num`), and the six category hues, which the store uses only as tint.

Logo. Shared by both worlds: the SiDragonframe dragon in white on a fire-gradient tile that runs gold (logo-gold) to orange (logo-orange) to red (logo-red) at 140deg, with a 1.5px white inner highlight on top, a 2px dark-red inner edge at the bottom, and a small drop shadow under the dragon glyph. The same tile, on a 64-unit square with 15-unit corners and a corner-to-corner diagonal, is the favicon (`public/favicon.svg`). The fire gradient is an identity mark, not a category fill: it appears on the logo tile and nowhere else in either world. Each world sets the tile's outer shadow; El valle's is documented in its Elevation & Depth.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (ground) with white rounded surfaces resting on it; deep teal rail as the frame.
Six flat category colours used as board spaces, chips, tags and card bands, always with a dark ink and a pale wash partner.
Nunito at heavy weights only (600 to 900); tabular figures for every number.
Soft teal-tinted drop shadows with a 1px line lip; the token is the only piece with a solid base shadow.
Spring motion: the token hops, the selected chip and active nav slide, cards drop and their colour band snaps shut.
Fixed 3-pip stock ramp (Bajo / Medio / Alto) wherever stock appears.

rules.name: The Board Space Rule
rules.body: A category colour as a flat fill means exactly one thing: this product belongs to that category. Fills are never gradients, never decorative, never reused for status (status has peligro and the pip ramp).

rules.name: The Fixed Board Rule
rules.body: Category fills and sol are the same in light and dark mode; only their ink and wash partners shift. Anything sitting on a fill uses on-fill ink.

rules.name: The Sol Marks Here Rule
rules.body: Sun yellow is reserved for current position and goal: active section, the goal flag, the one accent action. If two sol elements compete on screen, one is wrong.

rules.name: The Heavy Ink Rule
rules.body: No weight below 600 anywhere. Labels and controls are 800, headings and counts 900.

rules.name: The Still Figures Rule
rules.body: Every SKU, stock count, price, goal, pace and time uses tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, letter-spacing 0.01em). Counters that change in place flip digit by digit (FlipNumber) rather than re-rendering.

rules.name: The Table-Top Rule
rules.body: Shadows fall down and are tinted by the teal shadow channel; nothing glows, nothing floats sideways except the drawer.

rules.name: The One Piece Rule
rules.body: A solid zero-blur base shadow belongs to the token, because it is a physical piece standing on a space. Cards and buttons never get a hard offset slab.

dos: Do colour a track space, chip, card band or tag dot only with the product's category fill, and pair text on it with on-fill ink.
Do set every number (SKU, stock, price, goal, pace, time) in tabular figures, and flip digits in place when a counter changes.
Do show stock with the 3-pip ramp (peligro / sol / turquesa) everywhere stock appears: table, stack, drawer.
Do keep type at 600 or heavier: 800 for labels and controls, 900 for headings and counts.
Do rest surfaces on the Card shadow and use sunken felt for troughs and empty states inside them.
Do keep destructive actions outlined, separated from the data fields, and confirmed (Cerrar lote, Eliminar).
Do use spring motion for things that move between places (token, active nav, selected chip, stack cards) and honour reduced motion.
donts: Don't build the category default: a grey table with one blue accent and a generic progress bar.
Don't put category colours in gradients or use them for status or decoration.
Don't give cards or buttons a hard zero-blur offset shadow; that base belongs to the token alone.
Don't set labels in uppercase with letter-spacing or add eyebrow labels above page titles; labels are sentence-case 800.
Don't use a second display face or weights below 600.
Don't let sol mark anything other than current position, goal, or the one accent action.

store.overview:
The store is a toy valley at dusk seen through a vine-framed window. The fire logo tile rises over the hills like the sun, embers drift up from it, toy silhouettes (a bear on the left hill, a block tower and a rocket on the right) stand on the ridges, and the catalog below reads like a game's world index: Lilita One category tabs between hairlines broken by a single dot, and framed card wells that are each a small piece of the valley at their category's hour of day.

The ground is near-black pine, never white. Light comes from two sources only: the authored dusk scene and fire. Fire is rationed: the gradient belongs to the logo tile, and one flat fire-orange action with dark ink leads each view. Everything else is white ink, sage and moss on pine, with hairline structure instead of boxed sections.

Confirmed rejection: the white e-commerce grid with a banner carousel.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black pine ground with pine surfaces one and two steps lighter; 1px hairlines broken by a single dot.
Lilita One display in white, moss for inactive tabs and the footer wordmark; Nunito body in sage or ink.
One flat fire-orange action per view with fire-ink text; the fire gradient only on the logo tile.
Card image wells with hand-cut organic corners and a 2px moss rim, each holding a per-category valley scene.
Category colours only as icon tint and small dots, never as fills.
An authored SVG valley whose hills, vines and grass are anchored to the frame's edges, with pointer parallax and rising embers that stop under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Fire Rule
rules.body: Each view carries exactly one filled fire-orange action with fire-ink text. Other fire on screen (count badge, seal, icon, caret, selection, hover text) points at that same purchase path and is never a second action. A secondary choice beside it is outlined (Comprobante, Volver).

rules.name: The Fire Tile Rule
rules.body: The gold-orange-red fire gradient lives only on the logo tile and the favicon. Buttons, badges and the seal use flat fire. The valley's own dusk gradients (sky, sun halo, hills) are scene light, not UI fill.

rules.name: The Dots and Tints Rule
rules.body: On pine, a category colour appears only as the toy icon's tint inside a card well and as the 10px dot on a season pill. It is never a block, band or panel; panel-style category fills do not cross into the store. The shipped sale sticker (a coral disc on discounted cards) is a known divergence from this rule, not a pattern to extend.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Lilita One speaks for whatever a family reads as a name or acts on: titles, tabs, prices, totals, numerals, links and every button label. Nunito carries descriptions, meta, field text and labels. Lilita has one weight; never synthesise bold on it.

rules.name: The White, Moss, Sage Rule
rules.body: Titles and active states are white ink; inactive tabs, the footer wordmark and footer links are moss; supporting copy is sage. Body Nunito never drops below 600.

rules.name: The Glow, Not Slab Rule
rules.body: In El valle, anything raised casts a blurred shadow or a warm glow; a hard offset base never appears, including under the logo tile.

dos: Do keep the store on pine ground (sw-ground) with pine surface and raised steps; never introduce a white or light surface.
Do give each view exactly one flat fire-orange action with fire-ink Lilita text, and outline any choice beside it.
Do separate sections with the rule-dot divider and move the dot between placements rather than adding boxes or borders.
Do set titles, tabs, prices, links and button labels in Lilita One; descriptions, meta and labels in Nunito 600 to 800.
Do frame every product image in an organic well with the 2px moss rim, alternating the two organic radii.
Do show category only as icon tint and small dots, and give photo-less products their category's CardScene.
Do anchor scene pieces that carry meaning (hills, toys, vines) to the frame's edges so they survive narrow widths, and keep hero text inside the deep-blue band of the sky.
Do stop parallax, embers and twinkle under reduced motion, and keep the ember focus ring on every focusable element.
donts: Don't build the white e-commerce grid with a banner carousel.
Don't use the fire gradient anywhere but the logo tile and favicon.
Don't put a second filled fire action in the same view, or set text other than fire-ink on fire.
Don't fill tabs, cards, bands or panels with category colours.
Don't give anything in the store a hard zero-blur offset shadow, including the logo tile.
Don't replace the authored valley with a raster or stock image.
Don't carry panel rules into the store (sol as position marker, category fills, the board-space track); this world has its own.
